summary: Windham County, VT: tower and cabin built in spring 1920 by the Vermont Timberland Owners' Association with the Forestry Department; now gone, removal date not found.

facts.design: Tower with a cabin (1920 description); the FFLOS index lists it as an open tower
facts.agency: Vermont Timberland Owners' Association, in cooperation with the Forestry Department (1920)
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks it removed and FFLOS lists it as gone; no year of removal is given in the sources read

access.note: Most of the mountain is Green Mountain National Forest land with public hiking trails to the peak (Wikipedia); the lookout site itself is not described

visit.trail_note: Public trails run from the Chimney Hill development to the peak (Wikipedia). No source describes the lookout remains.

events.note: Spring 1920: tower and cabin built by the Vermont Timberland Owners' Association in cooperation with the Forestry Department, as quoted from History of Forestry in Vermont

evidence.supports: built in spring 1920 by the Vermont Timberland Owners' Association with the Forestry Department
evidence.quote: In the spring of 1920 the Vermont Timberland Owners' Association, in cooperation with the Forestry Department, built a tower and cabin on Haystack.

evidence.supports: Vermont Phoenix, August 15, 1924: height of about 3,700 feet, Wilmington
evidence.quote: Haystack mountain in Wilmington, elevation about 3,700 feet.
Haystack Mountain Windham 42.91389 -72.91915 Open Tower Gone
It has a summit of 3,445 feet (1,049 m) and shares a ridgeline with neighboring Mt. Snow to the north.

evidence.supports: most of the mountain is in the Green Mountain National Forest
evidence.quote: The remaining, and majority of Haystack Mountain is part of the Green Mountain National Forest.

evidence.supports: public trails to the peak from Chimney Hill
evidence.quote: Hiking trails are available to the public from the Chimney Hill development to the peak.

notes_for_editor: Build date rests on one secondary quotation (History of Forestry in Vermont, via Forest Lookouts); no primary report read. Record kind 'platform' fits FFLOS 'Open Tower' (vocab: open tower or platform, no cab), but the 1920 text says 'tower and cabin', so whether a cab sat on the tower is unclear; not corrected. Elevation conflict unresolved: 1924 Vermont Phoenix about 3,700 ft vs Wikipedia 3,445 ft. Removal is undated, so no 'removed' event is recorded (events need a year). Access: the summit is reachable on public trails, but no source describes the lookout site. Budget: 2 WebSearch calls, 4 page reads (Forest Lookouts, FFLOS index, Wikipedia, plus one secondary article grep). No photos found.
